name: Aider

surfaces.label: aider --gui / --browser: same Python process, hosts a Streamlit server (Streamlit's own default port 8501; aider sets no port) and opens the browser. Listed before the tui surface because the probe keeps the first surface that matches. Users who type `--browser` instead of `--gui` fall through to the tui surface.

aider --gui with plain pip or a framework Python: python whose arguments contain both the console script path /bin/aider and --gui. Needed because on a macOS framework Python the executable in ps is .../Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python, not the venv path, so the first gui surface cannot match. Listed before every tui surface because the probe keeps the first surface that matches.

aider in a terminal, installed into its own virtualenv by the official installer (uv tool), by pipx, or by Homebrew. aider is a Python console script: the executable in ps is the venv's python and the script path (~/.local/bin/aider) is argv[1]. Nothing on macOS is named `aider` in the process table.

aider installed with plain pip into some other interpreter (system, pyenv, conda, a project venv): matched as any python whose arguments contain the console script path /bin/aider. `python -m aider` is NOT matched (args_contain is substring AND, so 'aider' alone would also hit `pip install aider-chat`). Known false positives (substring match, cannot be anchored to end of argument): any python script whose path contains /bin/aider as a prefix, such as the official helper `aider-install` (~/.local/bin/aider-install) or an unrelated ~/bin/aider-notify.py. Also the likely landing surface for Homebrew and pipx installs on a framework Python (see notes).

working_signals.name: established TCP connection to the LLM API host with bytes moving
working_signals.meaning: aider makes the model call in-process (litellm), so there is no child process for a turn. A live HTTPS stream from the process is the closest direct signal. Inferred from source, not observed; a kept-alive idle connection can stay ESTABLISHED, so require traffic, not just the socket.

children exist only for git (GitPython), /run and ! commands (pexpect or subprocess), --lint-cmd / --test-cmd, and the notification command. Precise for the tool phase, blind to plain model streaming.

while a reply streams, a spinner thread and a rich Markdown live renderer run; at the input prompt the process is blocked in prompt_toolkit and sits near 0. The 3 percent floor is a guess (inferred, not measured).

WEAK. .aider.chat.history.md gets the user prompt when it is submitted (turn start) and the assistant text only when the reply has finished (turn end). Nothing is written while streaming, so a long turn goes quiet after 20 s. Also true for up to 20 s after a turn ends.

waiting_signals.meaning: opt-in only. Requires --notifications; --notifications-command alone is ignored (io.py ring_bell checks self.notifications). With --notifications and no command, aider uses the OS default, and runs it (default on macOS: terminal-notifier, else `osascript -e 'display notification "Aider is waiting for your input" with title "Aider"'`) the next time it asks the human anything after an LLM call started: the main input prompt AND y/n or free-text confirmations (add file, run command, apply URL). A short-lived osascript or terminal-notifier child of the aider process is the trace. Not a hook API, just a shell command.

without --notifications there is no external signal. Idle at the prompt and blocked on a confirmation both look the same from outside: process blocked reading the tty, near zero CPU, no children, no writes.

hooks.config: No lifecycle hooks. Nearest equivalents in .aider.conf.yml / CLI flags / AIDER_* env vars: notifications-command (fires when aider waits for the human), lint-cmd and test-cmd with auto-lint / auto-test (fire after edits), analytics-log (JSONL file)

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry anywhere in the source (grep for otel/opentelemetry finds nothing; issue Aider-AI/aider#4360 asking for it is open). Only opt-in PostHog analytics (--analytics, --analytics-posthog-host) and a local JSONL file via --analytics-log FILE / AIDER_ANALYTICS_LOG. That file works even with analytics disabled and records event=message_send_starting at turn start and event=message_send (or message_send_exception) at turn end: the most exact start/end pair aider offers, but you must launch aider with the flag.

notes: Not installed here, so no surface was classified live and every process pattern is inferred from install scripts, source and an analogous uv tool. Aider has no session ids, no per-session files, no hooks and no telemetry; a process maps to its transcript only through cwd -> git root. Working detection is heuristic. In tools/agents_probe.py only tree_cpu and tool_children are evaluated for this row: transcript_write needs a session id (per_session has none, so age is None) and socket_activity is not implemented, so both are documentation for a future detector. Matcher caveats: (1) on a framework Python (python.org, Homebrew python@3.12 venvs) ps most likely shows .../Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python as the executable, so the Cellar and pipx path_contains entries may never fire and those installs are caught by the name-based surfaces via /bin/aider in argv (not observed for aider). (2) /bin/aider is a substring, so `aider-install` and any /bin/aider* script also match the pip surfaces. (3) A gui launch on a framework Python is caught by the second gui surface only if --gui is spelled out; --browser is classified tui. The two exact options need launch flags: --notifications-command (waiting; note --notifications-command alone does nothing, ring_bell requires --notifications, and --notifications alone uses the OS default command) and --analytics-log (turn start/end). Docker use (paulgauthier/aider) shows only com.docker processes on the host. Watch mode (--watch-files) is the same process.
